# Story 07 — Admin Screening Management (Story: 7)

## Prerequisites

- Story 06 (Admin Movie Management) and the movies/halls admin stories are completed: `src/app/features/admin/movies/movie.service.ts`, `src/app/features/admin/movies/movie.models.ts`, `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall.service.ts`, and `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall.models.ts` exist and expose working CRUD/active-listing calls against the backend. This story **must reuse** those services rather than duplicating HTTP calls, per the intake's "Angular Structure" note.
- `src/app/features/admin/admin.routes.ts` already defines the `admin` route tree, including a placeholder `screenings` route backed by `src/app/features/admin/screenings/screenings.component.ts` (a stub component with matching `.html`/`.css`/`.spec.ts`). This story replaces that placeholder with real list/create/details routes.
- `src/app/core/auth/admin.guard.ts` and `src/app/core/auth/auth.interceptor.ts` already enforce authenticated-admin access and JWT attachment/401 handling for all admin HTTP calls; no changes to auth wiring are required.
- Sibling plans in `.squad/plans/admin-dashboard/` for the movie and hall management stories establish the pattern this story follows (service + models + list/create/details components + a shared `*-error.util.ts` for backend error mapping, mirroring `src/app/features/admin/movies/movie-error.util.ts` and `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall-error.util.ts`). Read the movie or hall create/list/details components before starting this story — the screening feature must match their component structure, standalone-component style, and CSS conventions.

## Story Goal

Give administrators a working screening-management workflow:

1. An `/admin/screenings` page listing all screenings, grouped by date, showing movie title, date, start time, hall name, hall type, and price, with past screenings visually distinguished and without reservation-oriented actions.
2. An `/admin/screenings/create` page with a reactive form (movie, hall, start date, start time, price) that only offers **active** movies and **active** halls, combines date+time into a single ISO `startDateTime` string, validates price (required, numeric, > 0), and submits to the backend.
3. Graceful handling of all documented backend error responses (400/401/403/404/409/500), with the 409 hall-conflict case surfaced as a specific, non-technical message.
4. Loading indicators for every async operation (movies, halls, screenings, submit) and a disabled submit button while creation is in flight.
5. A post-creation success flow: success message, then navigation to the screening list (or a details view) with the new screening visible.

Out of scope for this story:
- Editing or deleting existing screenings (the intake only requires **create** and **view**).
- A calendar UI — a grouped list/table view satisfies the intake's "table, calendar, or grouped list" flexibility clause.
- Any backend change: conflict detection, active/inactive enforcement, and timezone-authoritative validation remain server-side.
- A global "all screenings" backend endpoint — the frontend must aggregate per-movie (`GET /api/movies/{movieId}/screenings`) using the active-movies list, since the intake explicitly says not to assume a global endpoint exists.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** `/admin/screenings` is a placeholder route rendering `screenings.component.ts`, which has no list/create functionality (per its ~366 B size, it is a stub).
- **New behaviour:** `/admin/screenings` becomes a real list view (grouped by date) with a link to `/admin/screenings/create`; `/admin/screenings/create` is a new reactive-form page; an optional `/admin/screenings/:id` (or `/admin/movies/:movieId/screenings/:id`) details view may be added if the executor finds a natural place to surface "the newly created screening" per requirement 13 — if a dedicated details route is not added, the create flow must navigate back to the list with the new screening visibly highlighted/present at the top of its date group.
- **Timezone strategy (must be documented in code comments where the combination logic lives):** the frontend combines the admin's local **Start Date** and **Start Time** inputs (both entered in the browser's local time, with no explicit timezone selector, per the intake's form field list) into a single local-time ISO-8601 string without a `Z`/offset suffix (matching the example payload `"2026-08-25T20:00:00"`), and sends that string verbatim as `startDateTime`. Do **not** convert to UTC before sending — the example payload in the intake has no timezone offset, so introducing one would silently shift the represented time. Document this decision with a comment at the point where date and time are combined (see Task 3 below).

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Screening models

Create file: `src/app/features/admin/screenings/screening.models.ts`

Define the DTOs matching the intake's "Screening Data" section and the create-request payload:

```ts
export interface Screening {
  id: string;
  movieId: string;
  hallId: string;
  startDateTime: string; // ISO local datetime, e.g. "2026-08-25T20:00:00"
  price: number;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
}

export interface CreateScreeningRequest {
  hallId: string;
  startDateTime: string;
  price: number;
}

// Enriched view model used for list rendering, joining screening + movie + hall data
// fetched from movie.service.ts / hall.service.ts, since the backend screening payload
// only carries movieId/hallId, not the movie title or hall name/type.
export interface ScreeningViewModel extends Screening {
  movieTitle: string;
  hallName: string;
  hallType: string;
  isPast: boolean;
}
```

Adjust field names/casing to match whatever casing convention `movie.models.ts` and `hall.models.ts` actually use (confirm via Context step 2/4 before finalizing — the backend example JSON uses camelCase `hallId`/`startDateTime`, but verify against `Movie`/`Hall` model casing for consistency).

### 2 — Screening service

Create file: `src/app/features/admin/screenings/screening.service.ts`

Implement, following the exact `HttpClient` injection and base-URL pattern used in `src/app/features/admin/movies/movie.service.ts`:

```ts
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class ScreeningService {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);
  // base URL constant: copy the pattern (e.g. environment.apiUrl + '/api') from movie.service.ts

  getScreeningsForMovie(movieId: string): Observable<Screening[]> {
    return this.http.get<Screening[]>(`${this.baseUrl}/movies/${movieId}/screenings`);
  }

  createScreening(movieId: string, request: CreateScreeningRequest): Observable<Screening> {
    return this.http.post<Screening>(`${this.baseUrl}/movies/${movieId}/screenings`, request);
  }
}
```

Do **not** add a method calling a global `/api/screenings` endpoint — none is documented in the intake.

### 3 — Screening error util

Create file: `src/app/features/admin/screenings/screening-error.util.ts`

Mirror the structure of `src/app/features/admin/movies/movie-error.util.ts` and `src/app/features/admin/halls/hall-error.util.ts` exactly (same exported function name pattern, e.g. `mapScreeningError` / `getScreeningErrorMessage` — use whichever naming convention those two files share). Map:

- `400` → "Please check the screening details and try again."
- `401` → reuse whatever message the existing util files use for unauthenticated (should already be handled globally by the interceptor, but keep the same fallback text for consistency).
- `403` → "You do not have permission to manage screenings."
- `404` → "The selected movie or hall could not be found."
- `409` → "This hall is already occupied during the selected time. Please choose another hall or time." (exact wording from intake requirement 8/14).
- `500` / unknown → a generic "Something went wrong. Please try again later." matching the existing utils' generic fallback message.
- Never render `error.error.message` or any raw backend exception text directly; always pass through this mapping function.

### 4 — Screening list component

Create file: `src/app/features/admin/screenings/screening-list/screening-list.component.ts` (+ `.html`, `.css`, `.spec.ts`)

Responsibilities:
- On init, fetch active movies via the existing movie service (Context step 1/2), then for each active movie call `ScreeningService.getScreeningsForMovie(movieId)`, and also fetch halls via the hall service to join `hallName`/`hallType` onto each screening, building `ScreeningViewModel[]`.
- Compute `isPast` per screening by comparing `startDateTime` against the current local time (`new Date(screening.startDateTime) < new Date()`).
- Group the merged list by calendar date (using the date portion of `startDateTime`) and render each group under a date heading (e.g. `formatted as "Monday, August 25"`), sorted chronologically, with screenings inside each group sorted by start time — matching the intake's example layout under requirement 11.
- Render columns/fields per screening: Movie, Date, Start Time, Hall, Hall Type, Price (formatted as `"150 EGP"` — build a small pipe or inline format function; check whether `movie-list.component.ts`/`hall-list.component.ts` already has a currency-formatting helper to reuse before adding a new one).
- Visually mark past screenings (e.g. a CSS class such as `.past` applied conditionally, dimmed/greyed styling) and do not render any reservation-related action button for them; still show them in the list per requirement 12 ("historical screenings should remain visible").
- Show a loading indicator while movies/halls/screenings are being fetched, an empty state when no screenings exist, and an error state (using `screening-error.util.ts`) if any of the fetches fail.
- Provide a "Create Screening" link/button routing to `/admin/screenings/create`.
- Do not include edit/delete actions (out of scope).

### 5 — Screening create component

Create file: `src/app/features/admin/screenings/screening-create/screening-create.component.ts` (+ `.html`, `.css`, `.spec.ts`)

Responsibilities:
- Build a `FormGroup` (reactive forms, matching the validator style in `src/app/features/admin/movies/movie-form/movie-form.component.ts`) with controls: `movieId` (required), `hallId` (required), `startDate` (required, e.g. HTML `date` input), `startTime` (required, e.g. HTML `time` input), `price` (required, numeric, `Validators.min` set just above 0 — e.g. `Validators.min(0.01)` — plus `Validators.required` and a pattern/`Validators.pattern` restricting to positive numbers if the existing movie/hall forms use a similar numeric-pattern validator; check `movie-form.component.ts` for the numeric-validation convention and reuse it, e.g. price field style similar to any numeric field there).

Show a loading indicator while these two calls are in flight, disable the form until both resolve, and show an error state (reusing `screening-error.util.ts` or the movie/hall error utils, whichever applies to the failing call) if either fetch fails.
- On submit: combine `startDate` + `startTime` into a single string in the format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` (local time, no `Z`/offset — see the "Product rules" timezone note above; add a code comment there explaining the no-timezone-conversion decision), build a `CreateScreeningRequest`, and call `ScreeningService.createScreening(movieId, request)`.
- Disable the submit button immediately on submit and re-enable it only after the request completes (success or error), preventing duplicate submissions per requirement 15.
- On success: show a success message ("Screening created successfully."), then navigate to `/admin/screenings` (or a details route if one is added in Task 6), passing enough context (e.g. via router state or by relying on the list re-fetching) so the new screening is visible.
- On error: map the `HttpErrorResponse` through `screening-error.util.ts` and display the resulting message inline on the form; specifically surface the 409 conflict message distinctly from generic validation errors (e.g. as a banner above the form rather than a field-level error), per requirement 8/14.
- Do not offer inactive movies or halls in the dropdowns under any circumstance (client-side filter), independent of the backend's own enforcement.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **No active movies exist:** the create form's movie dropdown is empty; disable the submit button and show a message such as "No active movies available. Activate a movie first." — enforced in `screening-create.component.ts`.
- **No active halls exist:** same handling as above for the hall dropdown.
- **Movie or hall becomes inactive between page load and submit (race condition):** the backend will reject with `400`/`409`/`404`; `screening-error.util.ts` must map this to a user-readable message rather than showing raw JSON — the frontend cannot fully prevent this race and must rely on the backend response.
- **409 Conflict (hall double-booking):** display the specific message from requirement 8 ("This hall is already occupied during the selected time. Please choose another hall or time.") distinctly from generic 400 validation errors, and re-enable the submit button so the admin can adjust hall/time and retry.
- **Price entered as 0, negative, or non-numeric:** blocked client-side via the form's validators (Task 5) before any HTTP call is made; verify the exact validator names/pattern used in `movie-form.component.ts` and mirror them.
- **Start date/time in the past selected by the admin:** the intake does not explicitly require a client-side "must be future" validator; do not invent one — rely on the backend's validation and its error response, mapped via `screening-error.util.ts`. Document this as an assumption if the backend does not reject past dates.
- **Timezone ambiguity:** since the combined `startDateTime` string carries no offset, a screening created near a daylight-saving transition or from a browser in a different timezone than the cinema's actual timezone could be misinterpreted. This is called out but **not resolved** by this story — the backend is the source of truth for interpretation of the naive datetime string. Flag this explicitly in code comments per the "Product rules" section.
- **Duplicate submit clicks:** guarded by disabling the submit button synchronously on submit (Task 5), re-enabled only in the HTTP response/error callback.
- **Screening list with zero screenings for all active movies:** show an explicit empty state, not a blank page.
- **Screening whose associated movie or hall was later deactivated:** it must still display correctly in the list (movie/hall lookups are joined by id at fetch time regardless of active status) — do not filter the list itself by active status, only the create form's dropdowns.
- **Grouping across many movies/halls fetched in parallel:** if one of the parallel `getScreeningsForMovie` calls fails while others succeed, decide whether to show partial results with a warning banner or fail the whole list — prefer showing partial results with an inline warning per screening-list loading-state conventions, since one movie's failure should not hide all other screenings.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `/admin/screenings` lists screenings grouped by date with movie, date, start time, hall, hall type, and price displayed for each.
- [ ] Past screenings are visually distinguished and show no reservation-related actions; they remain visible in the list.
- [ ] `/admin/screenings/create` renders a reactive form with movie, hall, start date, start time, and price fields.
- [ ] Only active movies and only active halls appear as selectable options in the create form.
- [ ] Start date and start time are combined into a single `startDateTime` string matching the backend's example format, with the timezone/no-offset decision documented in code comments.
- [ ] Price validation rejects empty, non-numeric, zero, and negative values client-side.
- [ ] Successful creation shows a success message and navigates to the screening list (or details) with the new screening visible.
- [ ] 400/401/403/404/409/500 responses are all handled via `screening-error.util.ts` with no raw backend exception text shown to the user; 409 specifically shows the hall-conflict message from the intake.
- [ ] Loading indicators appear while movies, halls, and screenings are being fetched, and while a screening is being created.
- [ ] The submit button is disabled for the duration of the create request to prevent duplicate submissions.
- [ ] The existing `screenings.component.ts` placeholder is removed or repurposed consistently with the `movies`/`halls` route-shell pattern, and `admin.routes.ts` correctly routes to the new list/create components under the existing admin guard.
- [ ] All new and existing frontend unit tests pass (`ng test`), and the app builds (`ng build`).
